paper.title_en: Escort-qubit-assisted optimization of superdense coding over noisy channels
paper.abstract_en: We introduce an escort-qubit-assisted protocol that restores and stabilizes the superdense coding capacity of a shared Bell pair in the presence of amplitude damping channel (ADC) noise. Charlie sends Alice's and Bob's qubits through independent amplitude damping channels with rates $\gamma _a$ and $\gamma _b$. Setting either rate to zero recovers the single-qubit-noisy cases; both nonzero gives the case where both qubits are noisy. In the absence of protection, ADC noise degrades the superdense coding capacity monotonically, driving it below the classical limit in the strong-decoherence regime and completely erasing the quantum advantage; the degradation is most severe when both qubits are damped simultaneously. Our escort-qubit protocol overcomes this limitation by coherently tracking the channel-induced Kraus trajectories during entanglement distribution: Post-selecting the no-flip trajectory projects the shared state onto a maximally entangled resource, recovering the optimal superdense coding capacity of two classical bits, independently of the noise strength and of which qubit(s) are damped. We further show, in closed form, that once all Kraus trajectories are accounted for, the resulting unconditional average capacity, $\langle C_{AD}^{e_ae_b}\rangle =1+e^{-(\gamma _a+\gamma _b)t}$, remains strictly above the classical limit for any decoherence strength and any noise configuration. These results establish the escort-qubit protocol as a simple, scalable, and experimentally viable route to preserving quantum advantage in noisy quantum communication networks.
